## TypeScript Best Practices

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { resetAndSeed } from '../support/seed';

// Off-spine (control region): archive all completed jobs in one action. Two finished jobs and one
// active one; after archiving the completed ones, only the active job remains on the list.
test.describe('bulk archive completed jobs', () => {
  test('archives every finished job at once', { tag: '@functionality' }, async ({ page }) => {
    await resetAndSeed({
      clients: [{ id: 1, name: 'Acme Ltd', email: 'ops@acme.example' }],
      projects: [
        { id: 1, name: 'Live Work', clientId: 1, status: 'ACTIVE' },
        { id: 2, name: 'Done One', clientId: 1, status: 'FINISHED' },
        { id: 3, name: 'Done Two', clientId: 1, status: 'FINISHED' },
      ],
    });
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByTestId('nav-projects').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId(/^project-row-/)).toHaveCount(3);

    await page.getByTestId('jobs-archive-completed').click();

    await expect(page.getByTestId(/^project-row-/)).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(page.getByTestId('project-row-1')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('project-row-2')).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(page.getByTestId('project-row-3')).toHaveCount(0);
  });
});

import { request, type APIResponse } from '@playwright/test';

const BASE = process.env.BASE_URL ?? `http://localhost:${process.env.PORT ?? 3000}`;

  const r = await res;

    const body = (await r.text().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 500);
    throw new Error(`seed contract broken: ${what} returned HTTP ${r.status()} — ${body}`);
  }
}

  try {
    await must(api.post('/__test__/reset'), 'POST /__test__/reset');
    await must(api.post('/__test__/seed', { data: fixture }), 'POST /__test__/seed');
  } finally {
    await api.dispose();
  }
}

content.text:
I added an "Archive all finished jobs" button to the Jobs page; clicking it archives every finished job at once. `bin/e2e` passes: with two finished jobs and one active one, only the active job (`project-row-1`) is left on the list.

**Server**
- **New endpoint:** `POST /api/projects/archive-completed` (`ProjectController`).
- **Service:** `ProjectService.archiveCompleted()` archives every finished job that isn't archived yet in one transaction. It writes the same `PROJECT_ARCHIVED id=<n>` audit record per job as archiving a single job does, and returns the jobs it archived.
- **Repository:** a new query, `findActiveByStatusWithClient`, finds the jobs to archive.

**Front end** (`projects.ts`, `project.service.ts`)
- **The button:** it has `data-testid="jobs-archive-completed"` and is disabled while the request runs.
- **The list:** archived jobs drop off it, or show as "(archived)" if "Show archived jobs" is ticked.
- **Messages:** a screen-reader-friendly status line (`jobs-archive-completed-status`) says how many jobs were archived, or that there were none. A separate error message (`jobs-archive-completed-error`) shows if the request fails.
- **No confirmation step:** one click archives straight away, because the test clicks the button once and expects the jobs gone. Archived jobs can still be restored one at a time.

**Two differences from the brief:**
- **No database migration.** The `archived` and `status` columns already exist (V12 and V18), so no schema change was needed.
- **The server is Spring Boot, not OfficeFloor.** "OfficeFloor" only appears in the Java package name, so I followed the Spring conventions in CLAUDE.md.
